reports.title: Pre-training in 3D on quantum mechanics
reports.question: Does pre-training a 3D transformer on quantum-mechanical properties help ADMET prediction?
reports.takeaway: Quantum pre-training beats training the same transformer from scratch on 14 of 15 endpoints, as the paper says. Against the field it is middling: roughly level with fine-tuned CheMeleon, well behind fine-tuned Atom-JEPA and Monroe + TabPFN 3.
reports.summary: QuADMET-Former pre-trains a 1.3M-parameter TorchMD-ET equivariant transformer on PubChemQC quantum properties — total energy, HOMO–LUMO gap, dipole moment, E3FP fingerprints and Löwdin charges — across ten released checkpoints, then adapts it by linear probing followed by fine-tuning. Both a fine-tuned arm and its frozen embedding read by TabPFN 3 are run on the authors' code and weights, against LightGBM, fine-tuned CheMeleon, Monroe + TabPFN 3 and fine-tuned Atom-JEPA.
reports.finding: Pre-trained LP-FT beats from-scratch training on 14 of 15 endpoints by a median +0.083 R², and LightGBM on 38 of 45 combinations. Against the pre-trained field it reaches the top Tukey tier on 5 of 27 ExpansionRx combinations, nearly splits with fine-tuned CheMeleon (15 wins, 9 ties, 21 losses over both data sets), and trails fine-tuned Atom-JEPA (2 wins, 35 losses) and Monroe + TabPFN 3 (10 wins, 33 losses).
reports.caveat: Six discrepancies between the paper and the authors' repository were found and are documented in the study README; the arms here use the released checkpoints with those issues worked around.
